newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks again end higher, foreigners buy.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks again end higher, foreigners buy.

text.p: Sri Lankan shares ended higher for the ninth consecutive session on Thursday, led by foreign buying of large parcels of selected stocks, brokers said.
The Colombo Stock Exchange all share index closed 2.2 points higher at 592.04.
For the first time in several days, foreign buyers and sellers moved onto the bourse, pushing aside retailers who have been driving the market with small quantities, they said.
Turnover was an active 89.3 million rupees, up from Wednesday's 13.2. Most of the volume came from three large parcels, two of them through pre-arranged deals.

The two arranged deals were for development bank DFCC, which rose 1.75 rupees to 268 rupees, and Richard Pieris, which gained two rupees to 102 rupees. One million Forbes Ceylon shares changed hands but the stock closed unchanged at 4.75 rupees.
Foreign activity amounted to about 85 percent of the day's turnover. Foreign purchases amounted to 69.9 million rupees, while foreign sales were 82.3 million rupees.
"It is a good sign to see buying and selling picking up," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena of Commercial Stock Brokers.
